After talking with several friends, they all encouraged me to start a blog about being a small time real estate investor, and how someone can get into this. I’ve done research like crazy over the years, and it took me to various places to find all of it. So, I thought it would be nice to share information and put it all in one place. So, about me. My name is Scine, and I live in the Pacific Northwest in the United States. I currently have a little more than $360,000 in rental properties.

When I started investing, I was making approximately $50,000 a year and had about $30,000 saved up in my 401k. One day in 2011, I looked at my 401k, and I wasn’t impressed. I did some back of the envelope math, and it looked like I was going to retire with around $100,000 in my 401k. Now, that might seem like a lot, but 100k in 30 years might only be 30-50k in actual spending dollars. I was getting eaten alive by fees and poor performance. Even during the housing bubble, my 401k was only making 2%. Not acceptable at all in my book.

So, what do I do? I looked at various investments and they all had downsides. But, my friends father had owned several rental properties and that seemed like the way to go. I’d have a tangible asset I could sell, I would make a profit on the rent, and a profit on the appreciation of the building itself.

After realizing that I wanted to get into real estate, I made a decision. I’d empty out my 401k, pay the massive tax bill for that, and go for it.

As you can imagine, I got a LOT of resistance from friends and family. "You don’t know what you’re doing". "You’re going to lose your ass". "You’ll have no retirement" they’d all say. But, I’m the kind of person who carves his own path, and I did enough homework to feel comfortable to make the leap.

To be continued.....
